decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up approaches to the two gold vehicles. Plan blue for vehicles, white for figurines, red for watches; geometry estimated from RGB.
Advance and lower above each gold vehicle, rotating the jaws toward the vehicle width. Use wrist views next to refine alignment before closure.
Wrist views show lateral offsets. Lift clear, center each vehicle between its jaws with small sideways corrections, then begin descent.
Fine-center, descend 24 mm and close around vehicle bodies. Start a small lift; retention must be checked visually.
Lift the closed grasps clear, then carry toward opposite halves of the blue basket while keeping arms separated.
Right vehicle is visibly retained; lower and release over blue. Left tank fell back onto the table, so return open for a deeper regrasp.
Correct the rejected tensor; no prior motion occurred. Lower the open left gripper toward the tank body and clear the right gripper from blue.
Replan from interrupted prefix. Smaller right retreat avoids a joint jump. Left lowers another 48 mm toward the tank's wider body.
Close deeper around the centered tank and test retention with a short vertical lift. Right approaches the green watch through clear space.
Tank appears pinched between both jaws; lift with the gripper closed and begin transport. Bring right above the green watch for visual alignment.
Tank remains visibly retained; carry toward blue's left half. Shift the right wrist toward the green watch and descend open, checking alignment before closing.
The tank dropped and is now upside down on the table; approach its new location open. Close on the green watch and test a slow short lift.
Refine left approach to the overturned tank using its current visible location. Hold the right watch grasp closed before a slow 40 mm retention lift.
Grasp the tank's exposed tread body and pause closed. Green watch remains visually fixed in the right grasp; carry it toward the red basket.
Test the deeper tank grasp with a slow vertical lift. Place the retained green watch low over red and begin release.
Tank remains fixed between the jaws on the lift; carry steadily toward blue without changing orientation. Green watch is released inside red; retreat the right arm.
Move the retained tank fully over the left half of blue and lower gently; keep closed until its placement is visually confirmed.
Release the tank over blue and withdraw open after a settling pause. The next left-arm target is the nearer left figurine.
Both gold vehicles are visibly inside blue. Move the left open gripper to a high approach above the left figurine; keep the right arm clear.
The figurine lies across the jaw opening. Reorient above it toward a more vertical, cross-body grasp before descending.
Finish aligning the jaws across the figurine's torso and descend cautiously. Keep the other arm stationary and separated.
Shift the grasp from the figurine's head toward its torso, lower slightly, and close without lifting yet.
Maintain closure and test the torso grasp with a slow vertical lift before transporting the figurine.
The figurine is retained after the lift. Carry it steadily toward the white basket with unchanged orientation and the gripper commanded closed.
Correct the rejected tensor, from the unchanged observation. Carry the retained figurine over white with the right arm stationary.
Replan after the continuity interruption with smaller increments. Tilt the held figurine forward into white instead of extending the wrist farther at height.
The figurine is over the interior of white. Open, pause to let it settle, then withdraw a short distance clear of the rim.
First figurine is released in white. Move toward the second figurine while gradually unwinding the wrist to a cross-torso top-down orientation.
Continue the high approach toward the remaining figurine at the centerline, finishing the wrist alignment. Right arm stays well to its own side.
Fine-center the remaining figurine's torso between the open jaws and descend 40 mm. Inspect alignment before closing; right remains clear.
Correct the close-range offset toward the figurine's torso, keeping grasp height nearly fixed. Close and pause before testing the lift.
Keep the torso grasp closed, pause, then test retention with a slow 60 mm lift. Right arm remains stationary.
The figurine rotated and is not securely retained. Reopen, shift from its feet toward the torso, and lower slightly for a deeper grasp.
The figurine shifted during release. Center the open jaws on its newly visible torso, then descend to grip below its widest surface.
Shift the grasp from the large head toward the torso visible below it, lower 8 mm, and close with a stationary dwell.
Test the deeper torso grasp with a slow vertical lift, keeping the opening command at zero throughout.
The deeper grasp appears retained. Lift clear and carry toward white, gradually tilting forward to preserve reach margin.
Correct the rejected tensor with no compensation; carry the retained figurine toward white, maintaining orientation and keeping right stationary.
Place the retained figurine in the left side of white, clear of the first figurine. Lower gently and begin opening over the basket.
Both figurines are visibly in white. Withdraw the open left gripper and approach the remaining watch; it will need a center staging transfer to the right arm.
Center the remaining watch in the open left jaws while descending slowly. Keep the right arm separated until the watch is staged centrally.
The watch is centered between the left jaws. Lower another 21 mm to engage its sides, then close and dwell before lifting.
Lift the closed left watch grasp to verify retention. Bring the right arm back toward a separated waiting position for the later center staging pickup.
The watch slipped back to the table. Reopen and approach its new position from more directly above for a deeper, centered grasp.
Center the silver watch between the open jaws and descend another 30 mm before closing around the band. Dwell before any lift.
Maintain closure and test the watch grasp with a short, slow lift. Retention remains uncertain after the watch rotated during closure.
The watch is not retained. Reopen, shift back toward the band center, and lower to engage the lower sides rather than the sloping top.
The descent displaced the watch left. Lift away from contact, then recenter laterally over its new position before another descent.
Use the now-centered watch image for a small lateral correction and a slow 26 mm descent, then close around the lower band without transporting yet.
Test this lower band grasp with a slow 45 mm lift, maintaining closure and checking visual retention before transfer.
The watch remains between the jaws after the lift. Carry it to a centerline staging location for right-arm pickup without crossing the arms.
Lower the retained watch to the centerline tabletop staging spot, keeping the right arm clear and the left grasp closed until supported.
Release the watch at the center staging spot, wait briefly, then clear the left gripper upward and left before right-arm pickup.
Clear the left arm farther into its workspace while the right approaches the staged watch from above, adopting a cross-band grasp orientation.
Approach the center-staged watch with a modest inward wrist tilt while keeping right link6 on its side. Begin returning the cleared left arm toward origin.
Lower and center right around the staged watch's band, then close with no lift yet. Finish the left arm's gradual return near its origin.
Keep the right band grasp closed and perform a slow retention lift. Make a tiny final left-origin correction while keeping its gripper open.
The right lift was empty. Reopen and shift the pinch toward the solid upper band, rather than closing through the watch's hollow center.
The jaws closed above the band. Reopen and correct backward slightly, bringing the solid band toward the jaw contact line; inspect before closing.
Bring the upper solid band into the right jaw contact region with a small backward correction and shallow descent; close and dwell.
The band pinch displaced the watch again. Lift open and change the jaw direction about the approach axis to seek a grasp across the solid case instead of the hollow loop.
Use the rotated wrist view to shift the right pinch toward the visible solid watch case, lowering only slightly while keeping the jaws open.
Fine-center the solid watch case between the right jaws, descend 18 mm, then close and dwell without lifting.
Test the right case grasp with a slow vertical lift while keeping closure. Retention must be established from the next wrist view.
The case grasp was empty. Reopen and adjust the case toward the actual fingertip contact line during descent, rather than the wider region behind the tips.
The watch case is now centered near the fingertip contact line. Close at fixed pose, dwell, then make only a 10 mm test lift.
The watch was displaced rather than lifted. Reopen and move the case toward the fingertip line with a lower, backward approach; inspect before reclosing.
Relieve the small table-contact residual and recenter the case within the jaws, then close and dwell at fixed height.
The case remains outside the closed pinch. Reopen clear of it, correct the lateral offset toward the case, then return gently to grasp height.
The case is visibly centered within the open jaws. Close gradually, dwell at zero, and test with only a 10 mm lift.
The case remains behind the fingertip pinch. Open and tilt the approach toward it while keeping the right wrist on its side, rather than repeating the same empty closure.
The case is now ahead of the pinch line. Partly unwind the tilt while descending more deeply, then close slowly around the case and pause.
Relieve the contact residual by lifting from the observed pose with the right gripper closed. Check whether the case or band is retained before further transport.
The lift was empty. Reopen and correct toward the case's current offset, then descend with jaws open to inspect centering at contact height.
Move the centered case slightly toward the fingertip contact line without further deepening, then close gradually and dwell.
